Flat-colour illustration for Keywright, a cosy fantasy shop game that people look at for hours. A script turns it into chunky pixel art afterwards, so don't draw pixels: draw clean, vector-like shapes, like a picture book printed in a few flat inks. No outlines or line work, no gradients or blended shading, no texture of any kind (no wood grain, stone speckle, fabric weave, hair strands, scratches, noise or brush strokes), no small scattered details, and nothing thinner than about a hundredth of the picture's width. Each material in two or three flat tones in big areas: a lit side, a shaded side, at most one small highlight. Soft, muted, warm colours; shadows lean toward violet, lights toward warm yellow; one gentle light from the upper left. Big, simple shapes with clear silhouettes; plain areas stay plain.
